steps.text: Gather all ingredients. Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C).

Bring a large pot of lightly salted water to a boil. Cook lasagna noodles in boiling water, stirring occasionally, until tender yet firm to the bite, about 8 minutes. Drain, rinse with cold water, and set aside.

Meanwhile, place chicken in a large saucepan with enough water to cover; bring to a boil. Cook until chicken is no longer pink and the juices run clear, about 20 minutes. Remove chicken from the saucepan and shred.
Combine shredded chicken, 1 cup mozzarella cheese, and cream cheese in a large bowl. Dissolve hot water and bouillon in a liquid measure; pour over chicken mixture and stir until well combined.

Spread 1/3 of the spaghetti sauce in the bottom of a 9x13-inch baking dish. Cover with 1/2 of the chicken mixture and top with 3 lasagna noodles; repeat. Top with remaining sauce and sprinkle with remaining 1 cup mozzarella cheese.
Bake in the preheated oven for 45 minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Creamy Chicken Lasagna
raw_recipe.description: This delicious chicken lasagna is made with tender poached chicken breasts, cream cheese, tomato pasta sauce, and lots of mozzarella cheese.

review.reviewBody: I was looking for a lasagna recipe that didn't use ricotta cheese (my brother refuses to eat it.) He absolutely loved this dish. It is a nice change from regular lasagna. The only thing I did differently was added some garlic powder, pepper and Italian seasoning to the cream cheese mixture, and also used oven ready pasta to cut down on cooking time. If you do try the oven ready pasta be sure to cover it with foil for the majority of cooking time, then for the last 10 minutes or so uncover to let the cheese get golden brown.

This was the GREATEST!!! Thank you so much.. I do have to give a warning though... a 9x13 pan is too big for this dish. Use the next size smaller for a BEAUTIFUL, full lasagna. It is sooo good and sooo rich! A dinner guest couldn't beleive that there was no ricotta in it. Thank you again!!!

We liked this recipe but only with the changes that others suggested, otherwise it would have been too bland. Cooked chicken in instant pot with 2 tsp Italian seasoning and shredded. Sauteed 1 onion, 1/2 sweet green pepper, 1/2 sweet red pepper, 2 garlic cloves and a few shakes of red chili pepper flakes. Added these to chicken once it was shredded. Used seasoned broth from cooking chicken (1/2c) plus added about 1/2 tsp of chicken boullion. Placed in 8x11 glass dish and it filled it up nicely. Used ready to bake noodles. Used jarred spaghetti sauce. Very good.

Made this last night and it was FANTASTIC!!! I basically doubled (tripled the chicken and spag. sauce) the recipe since I cook on Sunday for the whole week and I was able to make 2 9 X 13 pans and a small 8 X 8 pans, we LOVE leftovers. I, too, put my chicken in the crockpot in the early AM and then just shredded in the afternoon before making, seasoned the chicken with garlic and onion powder. I added sautéed chopped white onion and threw in raw mushrooms like a few reviewers suggested and just used Prego for the sauce. Used reduced fat cream cheese and went light on the mozzarella to try to make less fattening. Also used no bake noodles. Hubby RAVED about it and honestly, what a nice change from regular lasagna. I like cream cheese but more in a dish than plain and not huge amounts and I thought the amount was just right, didn't seem overly "cream cheesey" to me at all. Layering is kind of a mess but totally worth it for this dish! This is one we will make often!! I definitely think you can add your fave veggies to this for added nutrition or taste as well.

Added heaping tablespoon of minced garlic and a 8oz can of pieces and stems mushrooms and used oven ready (no boil) lasagna noodles. Covered it and cooked it 20 minutes at 375, then uncovered and cooked for 30 additional minutes. Turned out perfect!

Very, very tasty! My husband and I don't eat beef much anymore, so I decided to give this recipe a try. I gave it four stars because I did make some changes to the original recipe. I baked a whole chicken and shredded the meat. I also sautéed some mushrooms and onions, along with four minced garlic cloves. I used 1 TBSP of Italian herbs, mixed in with the cream cheese. And I chopped about two cups of fresh spinach and added those to the layers. I ended up using about 1 1/2 jars of spaghetti sauce, too. But it made a large 9X13" dish. Definitely a keeper!

Pretty good I used oven ready noodles and it worked just fine! I also added spinach and spices! It was really good! You can also use precooked frozen chicken to make it go faster! I made it in about an hour and a half total even using my short cuts!

I used lots of left over turkey from Christmas. I brought in a 11 3/4" roasting tin last night to a girl's Xmas get together (there was still LOTS of kids and one man lol) I slow cooked the turkey in chicken broth, garlic and italian seasoning as suggested. It shredded perfectly. I then threw it in my stand mixer with a package of dry Italian dressing mix, 2 packages low fat cream cheese and loads of chopped mushrooms. For the sauce I mixed 1 jar of Rosee and 1 tomato and basil spaghetti sauce. Layered it 3-4 times. It was gone in seconds!! The host's husband accused me of purchasing it from Costco or something haha

I think the recipe is great as written. I just wanted to experiment a little so I sautéed about a pound of mushrooms with fresh garlic. After spreading the mixture of chicken and cheese I spooned a layer of the sautéed mushrooms onto the chicken mixture before topping with the lasagna noodles. I did use 5 noodles per layer because I thought 3 noodles would be a little sparse. No other changes made. It came out wonderful and with just the 2 of us at home, I am sure the leftovers will be fantastic.

Holy cow this is good! I followed the advice of another poster who said she poached a frozen chicken. In my water, I added salt, onions, salt, and bay leaves. Let it simmer for 2 hours. I also made my own sauce with tomato sauce, olive oil, garlic, onions, oregano, italian seasonings, salt, and pepper. I also added mushrooms into the sauce and had some broccoli left in the fridge that I chopped up and threw in there as well. I used 9 no boil pasta noodles, making it three layers. I also used only 3/4 of the cream cheese because that's all I had. And on top of the lasagna, I sprinkled Kraft shredded cheese that contains parmesan, romano and asiago over the mozzarella. Baked for about 40 minutes covered, then uncovered and broiled for 5. My husband and I both loved it and lucky for us, we had leftovers for dinner the next day!
**EDIT** I just wanted to come back to this recipe and update on how many people rave about this meal when I make it. I have now made it for several friends and family members at dinner parties and it has been dubbed as my "signature lasagna dish". I have never made a different lasagna since finding this recipe over a year ago because it is just THAT GOOD. And the fact that it is truly so SIMPLE to do makes it even better. I even stopped making my own sauce when I make this because I have noticed it tastes fabulous even if you use pre-made pasta sauce (Preggo traditional is the best!!). If you're on the fence about making this, just do it! Your taste buds

This was a super easy lasagna and even though I think it did need a little more flavor to be a 5 star, it still made a great meal. I did change a few things and added a little more seasonings for my liking. I used oven ready lasagna noodles and used one size smaller pan than the 9x13, because this makes a smaller lasagna. Instead of making the chicken bouillon and water separately, I made up extra to use to poach the chicken in. I also added in some chopped onion and garlic to the chicken water, to add into the filling as well. Once the chicken was done, I used the leftover water that the chicken and veggies were poached in, to add to the filling. I also added in some parsley, italian seasonings, and some garlic powder to the filling. Once it was done we had a salad on the side and it made a great meal. If I make again, I would add in some spinach to the filling, because spinach would be excellent in this. Thank you for the recipe!

For any lasagna. I use regular lasagna noodles, UNCOOKED!!! I just make sure to add more liquid in with the sauce. The noodles absorb the extra liquid and make it a firmer dish!!! Also add fresh sliced mushrooms and garlic powder!

This was incredible this is a wonderful new way to make lasagna. Instead of boiling the noodles I put them on a baking sheet and added hot tap water, 10 minutes to soft noodles drain on paper towels. I will definitely be making this again. Thank you!
Made this multiple times now it is my favourite recipe ever

This is such a delicious alternative to regular lasagna. I actually found the flavors more mellow and less acidic than the usual ricotta/tomato combination, which I preferred. Would love to have had some spinach in there too, so will add that next time.
What a great recipe! I added a little sweet basil and it came out so good. Thanks for sharing this recipe it's a keeper
I make this dish not often enough. We both love it. Didn’t need additional garlic, there’s enough in the spaghetti sauce.
One of our favorites! I add a can of chopped chilis for a little zing (and usually throw in some frozen veggies 🤫😄).
This turned out great!! Only change I made was I used left over turkey from Thanksgiving.
